oneOf.description: Markdown, rendered in the app's own style.
A whole HTML page, rendered sandboxed: its scripts run, with no network and no reach into the app.

ArtifactName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters

ArtifactPublishCall.description:
`artifact_publish`: a lead, task or Navi publishes a report in its project's chat. With `path`, the agent's own
fleetd tool reads the file and sends it as `content`; the hub takes `content` only.

content.description: The whole document. Give this or `path`.

format.description: `md` or `html`; absent, `html` for a `.html` or `.htm` path, else `md`.

name.description: Its name in the project, which links use: `sweep-report`. The same name again keeps a new version.

path.description: A file to publish instead of `content`: relative to your working directory, or absolute.

title.description: What the person reads in the chat and the tab: `Dependency sweep, November`.

AskLeadCall.description:
A worker's question for its lead (the `ask_lead` MCP tool). The lead is woken with it and answers with
`message_agent`, which reaches the worker as a steer; the worker carries on meanwhile.

AutomationConfirmCall.description:
`automation_confirm`: a Navi asks the person to let one of its automations run on its own. The person sees a card
with its name, prompt and schedule; their approval marks it `confirmed`, which no lead call does itself.

AutomationCreateCall.description:
`automation_create`: a new automation in the lead's project. A webhook is added in the app, where a person sees
its secret URL.

schedule.description: Absent: it runs only on Run now (and a webhook, once a person adds one).

AutomationListCall.description: `automation_list`: the project's automations with their last run.

AutomationPauseCall.description:
`automation_pause`: paused true stops its schedule and webhook; false resumes them. Only an older node sends it:
agent-mcp lists `automation_update {paused}` instead, and sends a lead's `automation_pause` there.

AutomationRunsCall.description: `automation_runs`: its runs, newest first; with runId, that run with its webhook body.

AutomationScheduleCall.description:
A schedule in the lead's calls: a cron or a one-time at, one of the two. A tz left out is the zone of the person who
last wrote in the chat (their app or phone tells the hub), else the hub's `policy.tz`, else the hub machine's.

at.description: One time, for a reminder or follow-up: a date and time such as 2026-11-03T18:00 in `tz`. It runs once.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron (or @daily, @hourly…), for a recurring run.

tz.description: An IANA zone; leave it out for the person's own.

paused.description: true: its schedule and webhook start nothing; false: resume it, its schedule going on from now.

BriefCreateCall.description:
`fleetd brief create (--workstream W12 | --text "<intent>") --json '<Brief>'`. Without a workstream it
opens one for the work the lead took from the chat; then it sets or edits the brief, and a draft moves to running.

asked.description:
The ask (`project_message`) this order is opened for, so its asker hears when it lands. With workstreamId, a
later ask folded into that open order: its asker hears it went there.

text.description: The order in the human's words, when this opens the workstream.

BriefReadCall.description: `brief_read`: a task's agent reads its own workstream's brief, whole.

BrowserCallFrame.description:
A browser tool call of an agent's (`fleetd agent-mcp`); the node names the session it comes from by the calling
process, as for a lead call, and answers it itself.

cwd.description: The caller's working directory: the node's calls to the hub for the session go out from it.

BrowserControl.description:
Who drives a live session's browser. A person takes it over (human) and hands it back (handing_back, until the
agent's next tool call sees the page as the person left it, then agent). While it isn't the agent's, the agent's
browser tools answer that a person has control.

BrowserRecordingEntry.description: A stored file of a recording.

BrowserRecordingPartCall.description:
One piece of a recording's file, in order from offset 0. A piece at an offset the hub already has is taken again
(a retry after a dropped answer); one past it is refused.

BrowserSessionCall.description:
The session as the node has it now: sent when it starts, when its state or control changes, and when its
recording is uploaded (`recorded`, with its files) or can't be (`lost`, with a note).

threadId.description: The agent's session the browser is for.

BrowserSessionState.description:
Where a session is. live → uploading → recorded; lost when the node could not record or upload it; expired once
retention deleted its recording (its row stays).

BrowserTakeoverCall.description:
The node's lead call for an agent's `request_takeover`: the hub lists it under "waiting on you" until a person
takes control or the session ends.

ChangeEnqueueCall.description: `fleetd change enqueue <PR URL> [--task T1] [--workstream W1]`. The workstream defaults to the task's.

after.description:
PRs, in this repo or any other, that must merge first: the train holds this one until each has merged.
Enqueuing a PR already on the train adds these to it, unless it is already being merged. Only PRs of projects
your person can see: one of another person's Only me project is refused.

ChatFileCall.description:
`chat_file`: a lead or task uploads a file it made (a PDF, a CSV, a document) for its project's chat, as
`chat_image` does an image: read from the session's own working directory by its node, any type the hub takes
([`AttachmentMime`]) with bytes that fit it, at most [`crate::mcp::ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES`]. A lead shows it with a
`file` block; unshown, it goes after 24 h.

path.description: The file: relative to your working directory, or absolute inside it.

ChatImageCall.description:
`chat_image`: a lead or task uploads an image it made (a screenshot of a UI change) for its project's chat. The
caller's node reads it from the session's own working directory: a png, jpeg, webp or gif by its bytes, at most
[`crate::mcp::ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES`]. A lead shows it with an `image` block; unshown, it goes after 24 h.

path.description: The image file: relative to your working directory, or absolute inside it.

ChatReadCall.description: `chat_read`: the messages around one of a Navi's own chat, in order.

before.description: How many messages before it; absent, 5.

messageId.description: The message, by its id from chat_search.

ChatSearchCall.description: `chat_search`: a Navi searches its own chat, all of it, by words.

before.description: The next page: the hits older than this message, the last one of the page before.

from.description: From this day (2026-10-20) or time (2026-10-20T09:00:00Z), in UTC. Absent: from the chat's start.

to.description: Up to this day, all of it, or this time, in UTC. Absent: up to now.

words.description: The words a message holds, every one of them, in any order and case: "dentist saturday".

ChecklistCall.description:
`checklist`: changes in order, applied together or not at all. With `replace` the list becomes exactly `items`,
all new (no ids); `replace` with no items clears it.

CloseCall.description:
`close`: the lead says a workstream is done, and why. fleetd records it and stops the workstream's agents still
queued, running or waiting, except the merge train's reviewers.

why.description: One line on why it is done, as the human would read it.

CommitSha.description: Full lowercase hex commit SHA, 40 or 64 characters

ConfirmStepCall.description:
`confirm_step`: a Navi's lead calls it right before the final Confirm or Submit click on a site that doesn't pay or
order (booking a table, cancelling a subscription, sending a form, an expense, a return, a post). The call goes
through the Navi's approval mode like a send: the checker's go, the person's approval or YOLO let it through, and
its answer says to click. A payment never goes through here.

button.description: The button's label, as the page shows it: "Complete reservation".

does.description: What clicking it does, in one or two plain sentences: "Books a table for 2 at Lupa, Sat 8 pm, under Sam".

page.description: What the page shows around the button: the details being confirmed.

screenshot.description: A screenshot of the page from `chat_file`, for the person's card.

site.description: The site the page is on: `opentable.com`.

DecideCall.description: `fleetd decide --key k --value v [--why w] [--scope project|workstream] [--workstream W12]`. Writes source "lead".

DecisionsSearchCall.description:
`fleetd decisions search "<q>"`, within the calling project's scope chain. A query that is a decision's id
(`D12`) reads that decision, when it is global or the project's.

oneOf.description: A Mac screen's only: one agent-desktop command, run by the Mac's node.

DesktopCall.description:
`desktop`: one action on the agent's Linux desktop or Mac screen session, in the words of Anthropic's computer-use
tool, plus `launch`, and on a Mac `agent_desktop`. Coordinates are in the screenshot's pixels.

coordinate.description: `[x, y]`: where to click, move the mouse to, scroll at, or end a drag.

text.description:
`type`: the text. `key`: keys as xdotool names them, `+` between those pressed together (`Return`,
`ctrl+s`, `alt+F4`; on a Mac `cmd+s` too). `launch`: a shell command started on the desktop (`xterm`,
`./target/debug/app`; on a Mac `open -a TextEdit`). `agent_desktop`: agent-desktop's arguments, its command
first (`snapshot --app Finder -i`, `click @s8f3k2p9:e12`).

DeviceCall.description:
`device`: an agent-device command for the agent's iOS screen on another machine than its own, which its node sends
through the hub to the node hosting the screen (node/device/remote.rs). The agent's `agent-device` asks for a `run`
with its arguments; its node sends the files the command reads first (`put`, a piece at a time), the command as
the screen's node will run it, then fetches the files it wrote (`get`). Never a tool: the agent's node refuses a
`put` or `get` from a process in the session. Between the two nodes each step goes `sealed`, so the hub carries
ciphertext alone, and the screen's node runs nothing that doesn't open.

offset.description: The file's bytes on the screen's node so far: each piece follows the last.

oneOf.description: Another step, sealed with the session's relay key: `count` numbers the agent's steps, each above the last.

FactoryStatusCall.description: `factory_status`: the other projects in one read, or the one named.

hub.description: A linked hub, by its label: its projects this project reaches through the link. Absent: this hub.

project.description: One project, by title or project id; absent, every project but this one.

FailureClass.description: fleetd's failure taxonomy for a run. The hub maps these onto its existing limit, park and doctor paths.

oneOf.description: A plan limit with a reset time: park and continue at the reset.
A short request-rate limit (429 without a plan reset): park briefly.
No account or provider behind a gateway can serve the model.
Not logged in, or the login expired: needs the runner's login on the machine. Never retried.
529 or 5xx after the runner's own retries.
No HTTP response after the runner's own retries.
The request itself is wrong (bad model, prompt too long). Never retried.
The agent's process exited or was killed outside an interrupt.

FillCredentialCall.description:
`fill_credential`: the node reads a 1Password reference and types its value into the page, only on the item's own
website, then submits the field's form in the same step; the value never comes back. From the first fill on, the
session refuses whatever would read a filled value back.

ref.description: A 1Password secret reference: `op://<vault>/<item>/<field>`, `?attribute=otp` for a one-time code.

submit.description:
False to fill without submitting, for a field before the last of its form (a username before its password).
Absent: true.

target.description: The field to fill: a CSS selector (`input[name=password]`, `#otp`).

ForgetCall.description: `forget`: the one entry that contains `entry` goes from its file.

entry.description: Words of the entry to remove, quoted exactly; they must match one entry of the file.

topic.description: Project scope only: the topic file; absent, `MEMORY.md`.

GatedRunCall.description:
`gated_run`: a request storing exactly this command, shown in chat with Approve / Deny; the project's node runs it
once a human approves, and the result arrives in a wake.

ItemKind.description: What a run did, one tool call or event per item. Outputs over 8 KB are cut to their tail with `outputOmitted`.

oneOf.description: Bash.

timeoutMs.description: The timeout the call states, in ms.

oneOf.description: Edit, Write, NotebookEdit.
Any other tool, MCP tools included. `tool_name` is the runner's own name for it; `class` says what it does.

class.description: Absent for a tool fleetd has no word for, and from older nodes.

oneOf.description: A permission prompt (`can_use_tool`) and how it was answered.
Context compaction (`compact_boundary`).
The runner retrying an API call itself (claude's `api_retry`).

retryDelayMs.description: The wait the runner announced before retrying.

oneOf.description:
The node continuing a run itself after the runner's own retries gave up (Overloaded, Network): `attempt` of
`of`, sent after `delay_ms`, because of `reason`.

`fleetd review verdict --task T4 --sha <head> --blocking 0 --non-blocking 2 --summary s`, the last step of a
review task.
The lead flags its message for the person's look.
A lead's or task's image for the chat, read from its own working directory by its node.
A lead's or task's file for the chat, read the same way: any type the hub takes.
A lead's, task's or Navi's report for its project's chat (hub/artifacts).
Made by the node for a session's browser, never by the session itself (the node refuses that).
Made by the node for a Navi's purchase_request and purchase_fill (purchase.rs), never by the session itself.
Made by the node for a Navi's request_secure_input and secure_input_fill (secure_input.rs).
Made by the node for its agent's session tools (machine_roles.rs): placed by the hub, relayed when elsewhere.
`fleetd mac`'s step, answered by the agent's own node, which never sends it on (mac.rs).
Made by the node for its agent's `fleetd mac`: the agents' Mac, and one step sealed to it.
The factory bridge (navi.rs): any project's lead makes them (D310).
A lead's read back through its own chat (hub/navi/recall.rs): any project's lead makes them (D310).
A lead writes one of its project's own skills (hub/skills/saves.rs): any project's lead makes it (D310).
A Navi's final Confirm or Submit click on a site, through its approval mode (hub/navi/confirm.rs).

MacCall.description: What `fleetd mac` asks of its own node, for the agent session its process runs in.

oneOf.description:
`mac push`: the agent's worktree as it is now (commits, uncommitted changes and new files git doesn't ignore)
becomes the agent's folder on the Mac.

`mac run`: a command line in the agent's folder on the Mac, run by its shell as ssh would. It starts and answers
with its job; `logs` follows it.

background.description: `--bg`: it runs on after the CLI stops following it. A run in the foreground ends once nobody follows it.

env.description: The variables the agent named (`--env NAME`), with their values: nothing else of the agent's crosses.

oneOf.description: The job's output from `offset` on (its stdout and stderr in one), waiting a little for more while it runs.
`mac ps`: the agent's jobs.
`mac kill <job>`.
`mac pull <path> [to]`: a file or folder from the agent's folder on the Mac into its worktree here.

`mac sim start [--device <type>]`: an iOS simulator of the agent's own on the Mac, booted, which `agent-device`
drives from then on. One per agent; the same one again while it holds it. `device` names a device type
("iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)"); absent, the Mac's plain iPhone.
`mac sim end`: the simulator goes. Nothing touched for 30 minutes, it goes on its own.

MacSendCall.description: Made by the agent's node: one step sealed to the Mac's node (`mac_where`'s key), for the hub to pass on.

threadId.description: The agent's session the node made it for.

MacWhereCall.description: Made by the agent's node: which machine is the agents' Mac, and the key to seal to it.

MemoryReadCall.description: `memory_read`: one of this project's topic files.

oneOf.description:
The person's own memory: how they work across every project. One shared `user.md` on a hub from before
people.
This project's `MEMORY.md`, or one of its topic files.

NudgeCall.description:
`nudge`: the lead flags the message it just wrote for the person's look, with what to look at. Only for a
showcase, something to try or a risk, never routine news.

reason.description: What to look at, in a few words: "the Machines page redesign".

PermissionDecision.description: A person's or policy's answer to a tool permission prompt.

ProjectMessageCall.description:
`project_message`: Navi writes to another project's lead in its chat, as the agent "Navi <its title>", never as
the person. The lead reads it as input, never as the person's answer or approval.

hub.description: A linked hub, by its label: the project is there. Absent: this hub.

project.description: The project: its title, as factory_status names it, or its project id.

PurchaseClaimCall.description:
The node's lead call for an agent's `purchase_fill`: claims an approved purchase for one fill. The hub refuses it
unless the purchase is this Navi's, approved, unfilled and within its window; claimed, nothing else can fill it.

PurchaseFillCall.description: `purchase_fill`: once the person approved the purchase, fill its card into the checkout's card fields.

requestId.description: The purchase's request, as purchase_request returned it: `Q12`.

PurchaseFilledCall.description:
The node's lead call once a claimed fill is done. `typed` false: nothing reached the page, and the purchase may
be filled again within its window.

message.description: What it filled, or why not, in plain words; never a card value.

amount.description: Its price in the total's currency, when the checkout shows one.

name.description: What it is, as the checkout names it: `Double room, 12-14 Nov, 2 nights`.

PurchaseOpenCall.description: The node's lead call for an agent's `purchase_request`: the call, the session it is for and the page it was on.

page.description: The checkout page's address, as the node read it.

PurchaseRequestCall.description:
`purchase_request`: ask the person to approve paying at this checkout with the Navi's card. Call it on the
checkout page, once the basket and the total are final.

PurchaseShop.description: The shop the lead buys from.

domain.description:
The checkout page's host: `shop.example.com`. The card fills only on it (and its subdomains) and in its
payment provider's frames.

name.description: Its name, as the shop calls itself: `Hotel Adlon`.

PurchaseTotal.description: The total the checkout shows, with everything in it (taxes, fees, shipping).

RecordingFile.description: The files of a recording, each scrubbed on the node before upload.

oneOf.description: `actions.jsonl`: one [`BrowserAction`] per line, in order.
`dom.jsonl`: one [`DomSnapshot`] per line, after each step that changed the page.
`video.webm`: VP9 from the node's own screencast of the page, 1280×800. Absent when the node has no ffmpeg.
`video.mp4`: H.264 from the iOS simulator's own recording (`simctl io recordVideo`), in its screen's pixels.

RememberCall.description: `remember`: one entry, appended, or put in place of the entry that contains `replaces`.

replaces.description: Words of the entry this one replaces, quoted exactly; it must match one entry of the file.

topic.description: Project scope only: the topic file; absent, `MEMORY.md`.

RequestSecretCall.description:
`request_secret`: the human enters a secret in a masked field in the app; it is sealed to the sink's machine and
written there (0600). The lead only ever sees its fingerprint, in a later wake.

envName.description: An env: or order: sink's variable, when not the one the key names.

key.description: The secret's name, a dotted slug such as "stripe.test_key".

sink.description:
Where the value is written: env:<machine>:<file> (one NAME=value line), file:<machine>:<path>, or
order:<machine>:<order id> (one variable of that order's agents on the project's machine, until it closes).

text.description: One line on why it is needed.

RequestTakeoverCall.description:
`request_takeover`: ask a person to take the browser over (a captcha, a confirmation only they can give). It shows
under "waiting on you"; the agent carries on, and its browser tools answer that a person has control until they
hand it back.

reason.description: What the person should do, in one line.

RequestWithdrawCall.description:
`request_withdraw`: the lead takes back a secret request it no longer needs (the human said so in chat), or a
command approval nobody answered.

ReviewReadCall.description:
`review_read`: every finding of the latest reviews of the caller's PRs, in full. A task reads its own PRs', a review
task the PR it reviews, a lead its project's; `pr` (a URL or a number) picks one.

pr.description: The PR: its URL or its number. Absent: a task's every PR, a lead's PRs in the merge queue.

ReviewVerdict.description: A review task's verdict (`report`, `fleetd review verdict`), the last step of every review task.

prHeadSha.description:
The head reviewed. The hub fills it in when left out: the head a train review round was given, else the PR's
head now; none for a judge, which reviews criteria rather than a PR.

taskId.description: The review task. From a task's session the hub fills it in: it is the session's own task.

message.description: The runner's own text (its result or error), then the tail of its stderr. Never rewritten.

model.description:
The model a gateway named, as the runner read it off the error: the one it has no account for
(PoolExhausted), or the one whose credentials are cooling down (UsageLimit, RateLimit). Set only from a
gateway's words, so on a limit it also says a proxy decided it.

resetAt.description:
UsageLimit and RateLimit: when to continue, as the runner read it; absent when the runner's words name no
reset, and the hub checks the login on a backoff instead.

retries.description: How many times the node retried the run before giving up (Overloaded, Network).

SealedForRunner.description:
What the agent's node hands the machine that will host its session, sealed (libsodium's `crypto_box_seal`) to that
machine's box key: the hub relays it and never opens it.

SecureInputCall.description:
`request_secure_input`: ask the person for something only they may give, filled into the page's field without you
seeing it.

label.description: What it is, in the person's words: `Passport number`, `The code texted to you`.

ref.description:
Fill it from this 1Password field instead (an Identity, Passport, Driver License or Social Security item's):
the person approves, then call secure_input_fill. Absent: the person types it.

target.description: The field: a CSS selector on the page or one of its frames (`input[name=passport]`, `#otp`).

why.description: Why the page needs it, in one line.

SecureInputClaimCall.description: The node's lead call for an agent's `secure_input_fill`: claims an approved 1Password secure input for one fill.

SecureInputFillCall.description: `secure_input_fill`: once the person approved a 1Password secure input, fill it.

SecureInputFilledCall.description: The node's lead call once a claimed fill is done; `typed` false gives the claim back.

SecureInputOpenCall.description: The node's lead call for an agent's `request_secure_input`.

SecureInputSite.description: The site the field is on.

domain.description: The page's host: `passport.gov.example`. The value fills only on it (and its subdomains).

name.description: Its name, as it calls itself.

SessionEndCall.description: `session_end`: closes the browser and throws its profile away; the recording goes to the hub.

SessionHost.description: A kind of session a machine can host.

oneOf.description: A fresh Chrome per session.
An Android emulator: the Android SDK, with KVM on Linux.

An iOS simulator: legacy (D298). No node reports it any more, and the hub places none: the agents' Mac lends
simulators with `mac sim`.
A Linux desktop: docker or Xvfb.
The agents' Mac's own screen: its `agents` user's GUI session, on the console and unlocked, one agent at a time.

SessionKind.description:
What a session drives: a fresh Chrome with an empty profile (`browser`, driven with agent-browser), or a fresh
`-read-only` copy of an Android emulator booted from its Quick Boot snapshot (`android`, driven with agent-device at
the copy's serial), or an X display of its own with a window manager (`linux_desktop`, driven with the agent's
`desktop` tool), in a fresh container or else beside a fresh home directory, or the agents' Mac's own screen (`mac`:
the GUI session of the Mac's standard `agents` user, leased to one agent at a time, driven with the `desktop` tool
and agent-desktop). `ios` is a legacy value (D298): past iOS screens' rows and recordings still read as it, and a
new one is refused with [`IOS_GONE`], since iOS simulators are the agents' Mac's (`mac sim`). Every kind shares the
session tools, the action log, the video and the hub's storage; only a browser recording has a `dom` file, and an
iOS one's video is `video_mp4`. A node hosts android sessions when it lists the `session_android` capability and
desktop ones when it lists `session_linux_desktop`; a Mac screen where its `mac` host check is ready.

SessionRouteCall.description:
One of an agent's session tool calls, which its node hands to the hub: `session_start` to be placed, and the rest
of a session the hub placed elsewhere. Refused when a process in a session sends it itself.

frame.description: The agent's call as its node got it, naming the agent's session.

sealed.description:
A `session_start` again, after the hub answered the first with `sealTo`: the session's secrets and relay key,
sealed by the agent's node to that runner. A `fill_credential` of a session hosted there: the value the agent's
node read from its 1Password, sealed to the runner, which fills it and never holds the token.

SessionStartCall.description:
`session_start`: a fresh Chrome with an empty profile (or with `kind` android, a fresh Android emulator), for this
agent only, recorded until `session_end`. `ios` is a legacy value, answered with the way to `mac sim start` (the
agents' Mac).

kind.description:
`android` for an Android emulator, driven with agent-device; `linux_desktop` for a Linux desktop, driven with the
`desktop` tool; `mac` for the agents' Mac's screen, one agent at a time, driven with the `desktop` tool and
agent-desktop; absent for a browser. An iOS simulator is `mac sim start` on the agents' Mac.

purpose.description: What you need the browser for, in one line; the person replaying it sees it.

SessionStepCall.description:
A finished command of the agent's that drove a session hosted elsewhere (`agent-browser ...`), which its node hands
to the hub for the runner's recording: a line in the action log, and the page after it in the trace. Masked with
the agent's session's secrets before it leaves the agent's machine.

item.description: Boxed: every lead call frame is as large as its largest call.

SkillInstallCall.description:
`skill_install`: a lead installs skills into its project, or for every project, from a source. Pinned to the
commit it fetched; the person updates it from Settings → Skills.

skill.description: Only this skill of the source; absent, every skill it has.

source.description: `owner/repo`, `owner/repo@skill`, a GitHub URL (`/tree/<ref>/<path>` too) or any git URL.

SkillName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters

SkillSaveCall.description:
`skill_save`: a Navi writes one of its own skills, new or changed, as a whole `SKILL.md`. No one approves it: the
hub keeps it as a new version with `why`, posts one line in the chat, and the Navi's sessions get it from their next
start. It is the Navi's only, never another Navi's or a project's.

name.description: The skill's folder name, also its frontmatter `name`: `weekly-invoices`.

text.description:
The whole `SKILL.md`: frontmatter (`name`, a `description` of what it does and when to use it), then the
steps.

why.description: One line on why: what it learned, or what the person corrected.

SkillScope.description: The hub's two scopes, which a person (and a lead's `skill_install`) writes.

TaskCancelCall.description: `fleetd task cancel T1 [--reason r]`. Interrupts the thread and releases its slot.

TaskKind.description: Every task gets its own worktree: a writer on its own branch, a reader or reviewer detached.

TaskListCall.description: `fleetd task list [--task T1] [--state s] [--workstream W1]`, within the calling project.

TaskMessageCall.description:
`fleetd task message T1 "<text>" [--now]`. A steer from the lead: a running task takes it in at its next tool
boundary (`--now`: stops its current step), a queued one gets it with its prompt, and an ended one continues in
its thread, which re-takes a slot.

TaskSpawnCall.description:
`fleetd task spawn --workstream W1 --title t --prompt p [--kind write|read|review]
[--profile <name>] [--pr <url>] [--qa] [--repo <name>]`. The profile defaults to the hub's default; one the project
doesn't allow is refused, and a review task runs on the default whatever it says. A review task needs `--pr`;
`--qa` marks a review task as a QA run.

notDuplicateOf.description:
A writer refused as a possible duplicate: the ids it was refused for (`T12`, `C7`), when this is different
work. Needs `notDuplicateWhy`.

notDuplicateWhy.description: Why it is different work, in one line; kept in the hub's log.

paths.description:
The files a writer will change, repo-relative (`app/theme.ts`, `app/settings/**`): matched against the work
in flight.

repo.description:
The project's repo it works in, by name: its worktree, branch, setup and PR are that repo's. Absent: the
repo of `pr` when the project has it, else the project's own repo, or its plain directory.

id.description: The tool_use id, or a node-minted id for non-tool items.

TodoEdit.description:
One change to the list: without `id` it adds an item (text required, state todo unless given); with `id` it sets
that item's text, state or link, or with `remove` takes it off.

link.description: Replaces the item's link; `{}` clears it.

TodoLink.description: What an item is about, any of: its PR, the agent on it (its task), its workstream.

ToolClass.description:
What a tool call does, in fleetd's words: the runner maps its own tools onto these, so nothing past it reads a tool
name.

oneOf.description: Reads a file.
Searches files by name or content.
Fetches a page or searches the web.
Keeps the agent's own todo list.
Calls a tool of an MCP server; fleetd's own is `fleetd`.

UsageResumeCall.description:
`usage_resume` for a lead: lifts the usage pause on the machine its project runs on (the only one it may name) and
sends every thread parked there "continue". At most once per 10 minutes per machine; recorded as the lead's.

machineId.description: The project's machine; absent means it.

WaitCiCall.description:
`wait_ci`: a task asks to be woken when a GitHub Actions run (its URL) or the checks on a PR's head (the PR's URL)
finish, or with `merged`, when the PR merges. Its thread then continues with one line: the outcome and the failing
jobs, or the merge (or why the PR won't merge).

merged.description:
A PR's only: wait for it to merge, not for its checks. Woken when it merges, when it fails on the merge train
(CI, review, refused) and when it is closed unmerged.

url.description: An Actions run's URL (`…/actions/runs/<id>`, anything after it ignored) or a PR's, in one of the project's repos.
